problem:
Title: Generalized Sum over Union of Disjoint Index Sets

Let $\struct {G, +}$ be a [[Definition:Commutative Semigroup|commutative]] [[Definition:Topological Semigroup|topological semigroup]].

Let $I$ and $J$ be [[Definition:Disjoint Sets|disjoint]] [[Definition:Indexing Set|indexing sets]].

Let $K = I \cup J$.

Let $\family{g_k}_{k \mathop \in K}$ be an [[Definition:Indexed Family|indexed family]] of [[Definition:Element|elements]] of $G$.

Let the [[Definition:Generalized Sum|generalized sums]] $\ds \paren{\sum_{i \mathop \in I} g_i}$ and $\ds \paren{\sum_{j \mathop \in J} g_j}$ [[Definition:Convergent Net|converge]].

Then:
:the [[Definition:Generalized Sum|generalized sum]] $\ds \sum_{k \mathop \in K} g_k$ [[Definition:Convergent Net|converges]]
and:
:$\ds \sum_{k \mathop \in K} g_k = \paren{\sum_{i \mathop \in I} g_i} + \paren{\sum_{j \mathop \in J} g_j}$
proof_numbered:
0001 | Let $0_G$ be the [[Definition:Identity Element|identity]] of the [[Definition:Semigroup|semigroup]] $\struct {G, +}$.
0002 | 
0003 | Let $\family{f_k}_{k \mathop \in K}$ be an [[Definition:Indexed Family|indexed family]] of [[Definition:Element|elements]] of $G$ defined by:
0004 | :$\forall k \in K : f_k = \begin{cases}
0005 | g_k & : k \in I \\
0006 | 0_G & : k \in J 
0007 | \end{cases}$
0008 | 
0009 | Let $\family{h_k}_{k \mathop \in K}$ be an [[Definition:Indexed Family|indexed family]] of [[Definition:Element|elements]] of $G$ defined by:
0010 | :$\forall k \in K : h_k = \begin{cases}
0011 | 0_G & : k \in I \\
0012 | g_k & : k \in J 
0013 | \end{cases}$
0014 | 
0015 | From [[Generalized Sum Restricted to Non-zero Summands]]:
0016 | :$\ds \sum_{k \mathop \in K} f_k = \sum_{i \mathop \in I} g_i$
0017 | and:
0018 | :$\ds \sum_{k \mathop \in K} h_k = \sum_{j \mathop \in J} g_j$
0019 | 
0020 | From [[Sum Rule for Convergent Generalized Sums]]:
0021 | :$\ds \sum_{k \mathop \in K} \paren{f_k + h_k} = \sum_{k \mathop \in K} f_k + \sum_{k \mathop \in K} h_k = \sum_{i \mathop \in I} g_i + \sum_{j \mathop \in J} g_j$
0022 | 
0023 | We have:
0024 | {{begin-eqn}}
0025 | {{eqn | q = \forall k \in K 
0026 |       | l = f_k + h_k
0027 |       | r = \begin{cases}
0028 | g_k + 0_G & : k \in I \\
0029 | 0_G + g_k & : k \in J 
0030 | \end{cases}
0031 |       | c = definition of $f$ and $h$
0032 | }}
0033 | {{eqn | r = \begin{cases}
0034 | g_k & : k \in I \\
0035 | g_k & : k \in J 
0036 | \end{cases}
0037 |       | c = {{Defof|Identity Element}}
0038 | }}
0039 | {{eqn | r = g_k
0040 | }}
0041 | {{end-eqn}}
0042 | 
0043 | Hence:
0044 | :$\ds \sum_{k \mathop \in K} g_k = \paren{\sum_{i \mathop \in I} g_i} + \paren{\sum_{j \mathop \in J} g_j}$
0045 | {{qed}}
0046 | 
0047 | [[Category:Generalized Sums]]
